parole.significato: big round poached or boiled bread dumplings from South Tyrol, made without yeast, usually filled with eggs, cheese and…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Bavarian [Term?] (South Tyrol, equivalent to German Knödel), from a diminutive of Middle High German knode, knote (“knot”).

parole.significato: type of curved cylindrical shape of short soup pasta, especially in Liguria; similar to elbow macaroni.
parole.testo: From Bavarian Kipferl (“kipfel”), a cognate of German Kipfl.
From a northern variety of Italian (compare Trentino salmarin), from Bavarian Sälmling (source of German Saibling and English saibling), a diminutive of Salm (“salmon”).
